topic: DP-3T: The Privacy-Preserving 'Digital Handshake' for Contact Tracing
target_audience: University students (Computer Science/Data Privacy) or Tech-savvy Public

sections.title: The Privacy Dilemma
lecture_lines: Public health requires tracking viral spread efficiently.
Centralized systems risk exposing private locations and identities.
DP-3T offers a decentralized, privacy-first alternative.
animations: Create two circle avatars: Alice (#FFD700) on the left and Bob (#87CEEB) on the right.
Display a central server icon (#A9A9A9) at top center with lines connecting to both Alice and Bob, labeled 'Location Log'.
Place a large red 'X' (#FF0000) over the server, then fade it and the lines away to signify decentralized shift.

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: Hashing & Bluetooth Beacons
lecture_lines: Hashing transforms data into unique, irreversible digital fingerprints.
Bluetooth beacons estimate distance without using GPS tracking.
These tools form the foundation of private contact tracing.
animations: Display a box labeled 'Hash Function' (#696969) in the center; a text 'Secret' (#FFFFFF) enters from the left.
A unique hexadecimal string '7d2...f0' (#00FF00) emerges from the right of the hash box.
Show a smartphone icon (#87CEEB) emitting expanding blue circles (#1E90FF) labeled 'Bluetooth RSSI' to measure distance.

sections.title: Phase 1: Generating Ephemeral IDs (EphIDs)
lecture_lines: Every day, the phone generates a new Secret Key.
This key creates temporary nicknames called Ephemeral IDs.
These IDs change every fifteen minutes for anonymity.
To observers, these rotating nicknames look completely random.
Your permanent identity is never linked to these IDs.
animations: Display a label 'Daily Secret Key (SK)' (#00FF00) at the top of the screen inside Alice's phone frame (#FFD700).
Show the SK moving into a 'Derivation Box' (#696969) labeled 'HMAC/Hash'.
Four labels 'EphID 1' through 'EphID 4' (#FFFFFF) emerge sequentially from the box.
Highlight 'EphID 1' and show a 15-minute clock icon (#FFFFFF) ticking next to it.
Fade 'EphID 1' and highlight 'EphID 2' to demonstrate the rotation of IDs over time.

sections.title: Phase 2: The Digital Handshake
lecture_lines: Phones exchange rotating nicknames when users are nearby.
Each device stores only the IDs it has heard.
No location or personal data is ever recorded.
This "handshake" happens entirely in the background.
Your phone only remembers "who" it saw, not "where".
animations: Move Alice (#FFD700) and Bob (#87CEEB) icons towards the center until they are close.
Animate a small packet labeled 'EphID_A' (#FFFFFF) moving from Alice to Bob, and 'EphID_B' (#FFFFFF) from Bob to Alice.
Show a list titled 'Local Interaction Log' (#00FF00) appearing next to Bob, adding 'EphID_A' to its entries.

sections.title: Phase 3: The Diagnosis & Upload
lecture_lines: A positive test result triggers a voluntary data upload.
Alice uploads only her Secret Keys, not her contacts.
The server adds these keys to a public list.
animations: Change Alice's icon color from #FFD700 to #FF0000 and add a 'Positive' label (#FFFFFF).
Show a document icon 'Test Result' (#FFFFFF) appearing next to Alice.
Alice's phone sends a green 'Secret Key (SK)' (#00FF00) to a central Cloud icon (#A9A9A9).
The Cloud icon displays a list titled 'Public Infected Keys' (#FF0000) and adds the SK to it.
Highlight the list on the Cloud, emphasizing that no contact details or locations were uploaded.

sections.title: Phase 4: Local Risk Assessment
lecture_lines: Bob's phone downloads the list of infected Secret Keys.
It re-calculates the nicknames those keys would have used.
The phone checks these against its own stored history.
If a match is found, Bob is notified privately.
All matching happens locally on Bob's own device.
animations: Bob's phone (#87CEEB) downloads the 'Public Infected Keys' list (#FF0000) from the Cloud icon.
Inside Bob's phone, the downloaded SK (#00FF00) is passed into the 'Derivation Box' (#696969).
The box outputs several 'Possible EphIDs' (#FFFFFF) which are arranged in a column.
Perform a side-by-side comparison between the 'Possible EphIDs' and Bob's 'Local Interaction Log' (#00FF00).
A line connects a matching pair of IDs, and a red 'Risk Notification' (#FF0000) pops up on Bob's phone.

sections.title: Summary: The Decentralized Advantage
lecture_lines: The server never knows who Bob is or met.
Your identity and location stay on your device.
DP-3T balances public safety with individual digital privacy.
animations: Display a large shield icon (#00FF00) in the center, with Alice and Bob's phones behind it.
Show text 'Privacy First' (#FFFFFF) and 'No Central Tracking' (#FF4500) appearing around the shield.
The server icon (#A9A9A9) appears at the edge, showing it only has random keys, with no links to people.
